title: Cohomology of a finite boundary
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ and a prime $\ell\neq p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $a_0:Z_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ be finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], put $Z=Z_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $\mathcal G$ be a $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf on $Z_0$ [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Then, with compact-support cohomology as in [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology],
$$
 H_c^r(Z,\mathcal G)=0\qquad(r\in\mathbf Z,\ r\neq0).
$$

proof.text: Write $s_0=\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. The finite map $a_0$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper], hence separated and of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]; it is quasi-finite by [pqf-lem-finite-qf]. Thus $Z_0$ and $s_0$ satisfy the separated finite-type hypotheses of [lem-zl-quasi-finite]. No smoothness, reducedness, or weight hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Tag 01WN, lemma-finite-proper; Tag 02NU, lemma-finite-quasi-finite; application to the structure map

proof.text:
Put $N=Ra_{0!}\mathcal G$, viewed on $s$ with its Weil structure. Use the all-degree cohomology identity in clause (1) of the statement of [lem-zl-quasi-finite]:
$$\mathcal H^j(N)=a_{0!}\mathcal H^j(\mathcal G).$$
A Weil sheaf has underlying object in the constructible heart [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex, def-weil-constructible-heart], so $\tau^{\geq1}\mathcal G=0$ and $\tau^{\leq-1}\mathcal G=0$; with $\mathcal H^j=(\tau^{\geq j}\tau^{\leq j}-)[j]$ of [prop-constructible-truncations] this gives $\mathcal H^j(\mathcal G)=0$ for $j\neq0$. The exact functor $a_{0!}$ sends the zero object to zero. Consequently $\mathcal H^j(N)=0$ for every $j\neq0$. This uses the stated cohomology identity, not the weight conclusions of that node or a torsion-coefficient substitute.

source.place: Proof (1), the displayed identification of all cohomology sheaves; finite-map specialization

proof.text: Let $X\in D^b_c(s,\Qlb)$ be the underlying object of $N$. The standard pair is a bounded t-structure with truncations $\tau^{\leq m},\tau^{\geq m}$ [prop-constructible-truncations]. If $X\in D^{\leq n}_c$ with $n>0$, then $\tau^{\geq n}X=\tau^{\geq n}\tau^{\leq n}X=\mathcal H^n(X)[-n]=0$ by step 2, so the truncation triangle $\tau^{\leq n-1}X\to X\to\tau^{\geq n}X\xrightarrow{+1}$ gives $X\cong\tau^{\leq n-1}X\in D^{\leq n-1}_c$. Boundedness and descending induction give $X\in D^{\leq0}_c$; dually, using $\tau^{\leq m}$ and ascending induction, $X\in D^{\geq0}_c$. So $X$ lies in the constructible heart [def-weil-constructible-heart], whose two classes are those of the standard pair. Unfolding these classes by [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure] (3) and then (2): there are $L_1,L_2\in\mathcal E_\ell$, an integral object $P_1\in D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_{L_1})$ with $\mathcal H^r(P_1)=0$ for all $r>0$, an integral object $P_2\in D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_{L_2})$ with $\mathcal H^r(P_2)=0$ for all $r<0$ (cohomology sheaves of $\widehat{\mathcal O}$-module complexes), and isomorphisms $X\cong(L_1,P_1)$ and $X\cong(L_2,P_2)$ in $D^b_c(s,\Qlb)$: compose the isomorphism to $(L_i,M_i)$ with the morphism represented at stage $L_i$ by the rational isomorphism $M_i\cong P_i$. Only these definitional representatives in the integral category used by that definition are used; no comparison with another integral category and no single integral heart representative is needed.

source.place: The degree-zero assertion: the geometric direct image lies in the heart, with definitional finite-stage integral representatives

proof.text:
For $i=1,2$, by [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] (4) and (3), $\operatorname{Fib}_s(L_i,P_i)=(L_i,A_i)$ with $A_i=\Gamma(s,P_i)\otimes_{\mathcal O_{L_i}}L_i$. By [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact], for the ring sheaf $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L_i,s}$,
$$H^r(\Gamma(s,P_i))=\Gamma(s,\mathcal H^r(P_i)).$$
The field $L_i$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{L_i}$ by [lem-weil-point-sections-finiteness] (3), so the termwise tensor product is exact [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] and commutes with homology [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology] (c): $H^r(A_i)=H^r(\Gamma(s,P_i))\otimes_{\mathcal O_{L_i}}L_i$. Hence $H^r(A_1)=0$ for $r>0$ and $H^r(A_2)=0$ for $r<0$. Since $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ is a functor, step 3 gives isomorphisms $\operatorname{Fib}_s(X)\cong(L_1,A_1)\cong(L_2,A_2)$ in $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(\Qlb)$. Let $(E,A)$ be any finite-stage representative of $\operatorname{Fib}_s(X)$. By [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category], an isomorphism $(E,A)\cong(L_1,A_1)$ and its inverse are represented at one stage $M\supseteq E,L_1$, and after enlarging $M$ they are mutually inverse there, so $T_{M/E}A\cong T_{M/L_1}A_1$ in $D(M)$. With $H^r(T_{M/E'}B)\cong H^r(B)\otimes_{E'}M$ this gives $H^r(A)\otimes_EM=0$ for $r>0$, hence $H^r(A)=0$ for $r>0$ since $M$ is a nonzero $E$-vector space. The same argument with $(L_2,A_2)$ gives $H^r(A)=0$ for $r<0$.

source.place: Apply the geometric-point coefficient functor to the degree-zero direct image; its integral and rational formulas

proof.text: By [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], $H_c^r(Z,\mathcal G)=H^r(\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{Z!}\operatorname{For}\mathcal G))$, where the geometric direct image is the underlying object $X$ of $N$. Step 4 shows that every finite-stage representative of $\operatorname{Fib}_s(X)$, and hence also its scalar extension to $\Qlb$, has zero cohomology in every nonzero degree $r$, both positive and negative. A zero coefficient space has only its unique endomorphism, so its Weil/Frobenius structure adds no further condition.

Let $Z_0$ be finite over $k_0$ and let $\mathcal G$ be a
Weil sheaf on $Z_0$. Then
$H_c^r(Z,\mathcal G)=0$ for $r\neq0$.

proof.text:
After geometric base change a finite scheme is a finite discrete space:
its cohomology is concentrated in degree zero, and the higher
compact-support groups of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]
vanish since the scheme is zero-dimensional.

blueprint.statement: main-20261015 lemma: arbitrary Weil sheaf on a finite k0-scheme

steps.1: Finite structure morphism, no geometric smoothness assumption
steps.2: Cohomology concentrated in degree zero, using a pre-existing general exactness theorem

tool_uses.why: Only its general cohomology identity for exact quasi-finite compact direct image is used on a finite structure map; no weight argument or unit step is replaced.
Generic finite-stage truncation compatibility chooses a heart representative of the already-computed direct image.
Exact sections at the algebraically closed geometric point convert the vanishing cohomology sheaves to zero modules.
Only the explicit flatness of E over its valuation ring in clause (3) is used.
Generic exactness of scalar extension by a flat module is needed in the point-fibre calculation.
Generic homology preservation by exact tensor is used to compute the coefficient complex.
